title: Extracts from Adam's Diary, translated from the original ms.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The story presents a quasi-systematic account of the pre-Fall order (Eve reasons about carnivore teeth vs. herbivore diet as a puzzle), lending an immanent, investigable logic. However, the governing frame is the biblical/supernatural Eden and divine ordination ('it is ordered that we work'), which sits closer to the mythic-supernatural than to imaginary science, leaving the cognitive status conflicted.

novum_candidates.description: The storyworld is a functioning Eden in which death has not yet entered, carnivores subsist on grass and flowers, and the Fall is enacted as a concrete physical transformation of nature (beasts suddenly begin destroying each other once the forbidden fruit is eaten). This deathless-to-mortal ordering of the natural world governs the whole narrative arc.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The reader recognizes the world through defamiliarized anachronisms (Niagara, KEEP OFF THE GRASS) while the naive narrator treats the deathless Eden and its violent unmaking as ordinary natural history, producing cognitive estrangement around the altered natural order.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The Edenic order and its collapse determine the overriding narrative logic: the Fall reorganizes nature, forces expulsion and labor, and frames the concluding reconciliation. The diary's arc is structured around life inside versus outside the Garden.

novelty.rationale: The world differs totally from the empirical norm: predators eat vegetation, death is absent from the Park, and the eating of the fruit triggers a world-wide shift into predation, mortality, and labor. This is a totalizing, world-altering difference, not an incidental device.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The narrator applies a coherent, systematic (if comically wrong) naturalist method: taxonomic classification, naming conventions, trapping to secure additional specimens, and anatomical inference. The reasoning is immanent and nonsupernatural.

novum_candidates.description: Adam, encountering his own infant son, cannot recognize it as human and subjects it to serial naturalist misclassification (fish, kangaroo 'Kangaroorum Adamiensis', bug, bear, parrot), treating the first human child as an uncatalogued zoological specimen.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: The reader knows the creature is a human infant, while the narrator's earnest pseudo-scientific classification defamiliarizes birth and family, generating dramatic-irony estrangement without altering the storyworld.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The misclassification sequence occupies much of the diary's second half and drives its comedy, but it does not determine the overriding narrative logic, which remains the Fall and the Adam-Eve relationship; it functions as an extended incidental episode.

novelty.rationale: The child is an ordinary human baby; nothing about the storyworld is altered by it. The estrangement lies in the narrator's ignorant perspective, not in any totalizing difference from the empirical norm. This is a satiric device rather than a world-altering novum.
